subject: Urgent: Post-demo capacity incident — hosted -> dedicated/private decision
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@shopnow.com>
Cc: Chris Diaz <chris@shopnow.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + next steps after today's demo

Hi Anna —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Great to see the ShopNow recommender use case — the latency goals and expected concurrency you mentioned (peak ~1.5k reqs/min with 2–3k tokens/session) are helpful.

Recap / immediate asks:
- You said production will start with Hosted API but you may need more isolation/throughput if traffic spikes.
- You asked about Dedicated pools and a Private VPC option for compliance later this year.
- Action: Can you confirm estimated steady QPS and a worst-case peak day estimate? That will help us model Dedicated sizing.

I captured next steps on our side:
1) I'll share a rough capacity recommendation and cost delta (Hosted vs Dedicated) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If you want, we can schedule a short call with Connor (solutions eng) and Rishi (inference eng) to validate performance assumptions.

Attaching the capacity calculator and a sample Dedicated runbook.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0142

Attachments: capacity_calculator.xlsx, dedicated-runbook.pdf

From: Anna Lee <anna@shopnow.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T20:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today's demo

Marissa —

Thanks for the follow-up. Two urgent items: we just ran the pilot in staging and saw a sustained throttling event during a synthetic spike. The app degraded for ~20 minutes and our SREs flagged it as high priority. I'm pulling logs now and attaching the summary.

Quick answers to your asks: steady QPS ~300 reqs/min, expected peak ~1.8k reqs/min during promotions. Token distribution: many shorter requests (150–300 tokens) but with a 5% tail at >1k tokens.

We need to decide quickly whether to push forward with Hosted (with request throttles) or move to Dedicated to avoid a production incident next week. Can we get an urgent runbook and an estimate for Dedicated capacity + timeline to provision?

Anna
Head of Product, ShopNow Inc
anna@shopnow.com | +1 212-555-0199

Attachments: shopnow_slo_logs.zip

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@shopnow.com>, Chris Diaz <chris@shopnow.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-29T21:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today's demo

Anna —

Sorry to hear about the staging incident and thanks for the logs. Looping in Connor (solutions) and Rishi (inference) to triage the throttling and give an estimate for Dedicated sizing + provisioning time. Laura — flagging as a potential SLA/priority escalation for ShopNow (large strategic account).

Connor / Rishi: can you review the attached logs (shopnow_slo_logs.zip) and confirm:
- Whether the staging throttling looks like capacity saturation vs misconfiguration (prefix caching, batching, timeouts)
- A minimal Dedicated pool config (gpus + nodes) to hit the 1.8k peak with the token tail
- Estimated lead time to provision Dedicated and options for interim mitigations on Hosted (rate limits, priority lanes)

Anna — we'll aim to have a recommendation for you within 8 business hours. If Dedicated provisioning is required urgently, we'll include timelines and a rapid-ship option.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Anna Lee <anna@shopnow.com>, Chris Diaz <chris@shopnow.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T02:48:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today's demo

Marissa / Anna —

Quick triage after a first pass through the logs: the error pattern matches queue saturation on concurrent KV cache warmups plus several long-running 1k+ token requests that block batching windows. Two observations:
1) On Hosted we can reduce tail impact with two immediate mitigations: stricter per-key concurrency limits (protects other customers) and an aggressive prefix cache TTL for these sessions. Those help but will increase 429s for ShopNow until capacity is added.
2) A Dedicated pool sized for peak (~1.8k reqs/min with 5% long tails) looks like: 6 x A100-equivalent nodes with optimized quantization profile — rough lead time to provision: 3–5 business days if we have contract/commit. Private VPC/on-prem would require longer (2–4 weeks) due to network & provisioning.

If ShopNow needs zero risk during promotions, Dedicated is the recommended path. We can also spin up a temporary burst Dedicated cluster (short-term metered commit) to cover the next promo window while we finalize Reserved capacity.

I'll prepare a short runbook and cost delta table and upload in the morning (ETA 08:30 PT).

—Connor
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Lee <anna@shopnow.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T09:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + next steps after today's demo

Anna —

Short update: Connor confirms Dedicated is the safest short-term option to avoid production incidents. Attached is a concise runbook and the cost delta for a 30-day burst Dedicated vs sticking with Hosted + mitigations. Key options:
1) Burst Dedicated (30 days) — provision in 3 business days.
2) Reserve Dedicated (monthly/annual commit) — best unit economics, 3–5 days to provision after contract.
3) Private VPC — compliance-ready but 2–4 week timeline.

Please let me know which option you prefer and whether you want us to start an expedited provisioning path (I can pull an approval from Laura and engineering). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min call this afternoon to go over tradeoffs.

Thanks —
Marissa

Attachments: capacity_report.pdf, dedicated-30day-costs.xlsx
